articleContract.title: As AI agents reshape the web, Google opens Gemini and Search to more apps

story.title: As AI agents reshape the web, Google opens Gemini and Search to more apps

facts.text: Google said meditation app Calm is another new partner on this effort, and that its app will soon launch on both Gemini and Search.
Google’s idea is to open its doors to any business or developer that wants to reach users through Search or Gemini by allowing them to submit their own connected apps and monitor their performance.
Google is making it easier for businesses to connect their apps to its AI experiences across Search and Gemini with the debut of its Connected Apps Platform.
For instance, you could connect to Canva to design a flyer, or to YouTube Music to build a playlist.
Developers can also choose whether they want their app to be available via Search, the Gemini app, or both.
These apps will now come to Google Search over the next few weeks.
Search today has fewer integrations, featuring apps like Instacart, Canva, YouTube Music, Yahoo Fantasy Football, and others.
Google did not share when it would become more broadly available.

To get started, developers would integrate with a cloud-hosted MCP (Model Context Protocol) server or Android MCP using the AppFunctions APIs, then use the Google Connected Console to register, test, and submit their app, Google explains.
The "more than 50" figure is harder to place.
PPC Land reported on August 12 that Google's own availability help article already listed 41 connected apps before that day's batch of 13 named partners, five of which were already on the list.
On October 13, Google said the Gemini app connects to "more than 40 apps" .
Today's post counts Search and Gemini together.
It does not say whether an app available in both products is counted once or twice, and the arithmetic from Google's earlier lists points to a total for Gemini alone that is already above 50.
Google is letting more companies build their apps into Google Search and the Gemini assistant, so people can do things like book a table or plan a workout without leaving Google.
For now it is a preview that opens in stages, and Google has not said what it costs, how it picks between competing apps, or what user data changes hands.
Access is opening in phases, and the post gives no fees, no list of markets and no account of how Google decides which app handles a request.
The second half of the post concerns the apps users can reach.

"To help users get more done, today we're launching the preview of our Connected Apps Platform, a unified way for more app developers to bring their capabilities directly into Gemini and Search," according to the post.
The pitch to developers is that a single build covers both.
For three of the four Gemini names, the news today is Search.
Adobe, Experian and Peloton were among the 14 connected apps Google began rolling out in Gemini on September 23 , a batch that also included Airtable, Linear, monday.com, Squarespace and Webflow.
The single build for two surfaces also fits what Google's leadership has been saying in public.
A developer registering once and switching on either product, or both, is that idea expressed as tooling.
Merchants reach shoppers through one system, and service apps such as fitness, ticketing or car rental now through another.
Connected apps change what an AI answer can do: instead of linking to a business, Search or Gemini can call the business's service directly.
When Google first brought Instacart, Canva and YouTube Music into AI Mode in Search on July 16 , AI Mode assembled a task and then sent the user to the partner to finish it.
Until now, which companies got that treatment was decided through partnerships announced in batches.
A console with a submission queue turns it into something closer to an application process, even if Google keeps the final say through review.
With no paid placement on offer, being a connected app is one of the few ways a brand can be present inside Gemini's interface at the moment a user asks for something it sells.
For brands, that routing logic plays the role ranking plays in search results.
The console's metrics - traffic, latency and error rates - tell an engineering team whether the integration works.
Neither the post nor the console view Google published shows any link to Google Ads, Google Analytics or conversion tracking.
The decision to build the platform on MCP follows more than a year of Google adopting the protocol piece by piece.
In February 2026, the Chrome team proposed WebMCP, which would let websites offer structured tools to agents instead of leaving them to screenshot analysis, page parsing and simulated clicks .
Today's platform moves MCP from a setting that individual users configure to the formal entry point for companies.
Users connecting their own servers is one thing; Google reviewing, publishing and monitoring third-party servers across its two largest AI surfaces is another.
Developers plug in via a cloud MCP server or Android AppFunctions and pick Search, Gemini or both.
What the post leaves out: fees, app ranking and data terms.

Meta's Developer Tools MCP launched on June 30, letting developers manage Meta apps through AI assistants, and on April 29 Meta opened Ads AI Connectors that let Claude and ChatGPT create and edit campaigns .
The protocol is becoming the common plumbing of agentic AI , with each platform deciding who gets to plug in and on what terms.
Google's terms, for now, are a sign-up form and a review queue.
Both routes rest on the Model Context Protocol , the open standard Anthropic introduced in November 2024 for connecting AI models to outside tools and data.
Google's platform accepts that standard rather than asking developers to adopt a proprietary format, which in principle lets a company reuse a server it already runs for other AI assistants.
The technical description fits in a single sentence.
Nothing goes live without review, though the developer, not Google, decides the publishing moment once approval is granted.
